description: Exact natural-language provenance rules and production calibration cases. Every case is prompt-visible and a regression contract; known-wrong narratives mark adjacent factual and presentation failures.

rules.title: Read the complete retained lineage
rules.invariant: Read every event in the complete frozen Trace component in chronological order; do not reduce provenance to the latest event or latest recorded reason. Complete input coverage requires every material phase in the narrative, not one prose clause per event.

rules.title: Explain the origin context
rules.invariant: When a selected Memory was derived from a larger Memory or another Context, name the retained source Context when available and preserve the specific nearby source content needed to understand the selected content's origin.

rules.title: Name how the standalone Memory arose
rules.invariant: State the recorded operation and material method that produced the selected Memory, such as sentence chunking, without replacing it with a generic created label.

rules.title: Narrate disappearance and return
rules.invariant: Preserve the order of every selected-Memory disappearance and return plus every material content phase needed to explain what changed. Mention a position transition only when order or neighboring placement changes the provenance meaning; omit incidental numeric movement.

rules.title: Keep sibling activity out
rules.invariant: A component event that changes only a parent, child, or sibling Memory is context, not a lifecycle transition of the selected Memory, and must not be narrated as though it happened to the selected Memory.

rules.title: Write prose, not an event log
rules.invariant: Synthesize one chronological natural-language paragraph; do not expose raw event labels, arrows, checkpoint identifiers, timestamps, transition counts, or a command inventory.

rules.title: Compress without truncating facts
rules.invariant: Use one or two complete sentences within the requested character, UTF-8 byte, or whitespace-delimited word limit. Preserve discriminating before-and-after content, the material operation, Context movement, and selected lifecycle before generic purpose, justification, or unchanged-status prose; never mechanically clip a generated sentence.

rules.title: Do not invent intent
rules.invariant: A directly supported textual role such as a hesitation may be described from wording and placement, but do not claim that the author intended a placeholder, judged content useless, or had another unrecorded motive.

rules.title: Keep unavailable provenance explicit
rules.invariant: Return no narrative when retained history is absent or hidden by a Grant; never fill either condition from current content or outside knowledge.

rules.title: Anchor changes in exact excerpts
rules.invariant: When the bound permits, quote the shortest exact contiguous excerpts that distinguish the earlier content, selected result, sibling result, or current replacement. Prefer these evidence anchors over an abstract paraphrase of what the text required, and never alter quoted wording.

rules.title: Match the prose to the operation shape
rules.invariant: Express Split or Atomize as one parent becoming the selected and relevant sibling results; express Edit as earlier content becoming current content; and express a derived-then-edited Memory as source operation and first derived content followed by its replacement.

rules.title: Separate Context movement from content change
rules.invariant: When retained evidence says a Memory was copied, branched, or inherited into another Context, name the origin and destination and state separately whether its content changed; do not collapse that route into a direct Add in the destination.

rules.title: Compress long history into material phases
rules.invariant: After reading every event, collapse consecutive or repeated edits that follow one semantic trajectory into one material chronological phase. Preserve the earliest content, the current content or its distinguishing additions, and every ordered disappearance/return cycle; mention an intermediate wording only when it introduces, removes, or reverses a material meaning rather than merely rephrasing it.
